title: Hive Entrance Traffic vs Nectar Flow
dataSources: Beehive weight and entrance activity (`beehive:weight`), hive climate (`beehive:climate`), brooder climate (`brooder:climate`), egg counts (`coop:egg`), rain-barrel level (`rainbarrel:level`), greenhouse climate (`greenhouse:climate`), orchard bloom observations (`orchard:bloom`), and milking logs (`milking:session`).
app: Homestead telemetry from beehive monitors, coop sensors, brooder controls, greenhouse sensors, rain barrels, orchard logs, and milking records streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT, LoRaWAN, and Home Assistant.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=beehive:weight
| stats avg(entrance_count_per_min) as avg_traffic_per_min avg(weight_gain_kg) as avg_weight_gain_kg by hive
| sort - avg_weight_gain_kg
description: Compares entrance traffic with hive weight gain to show when busy bees are actually bringing nectar home.
value: Traffic alone can be misleading, and pairing it with weight gain gives a better picture of true forage success.
implementation: Record entrance counts and periodic hive weight deltas from your bee-monitoring stack and compare hives side by side.
visualization: Scatter plot of average entrance traffic versus average weight gain by hive.
grandmaExplanation: It spots whether lots of bee traffic is actually turning into more honey and nectar coming into the hive.
